goal:
Complete the remaining proof obligation in the seeded invoice reconciliation CLI. The current repaired implementation passes all 70 independent checks, including invalid currency types; do not change its behavior, remove assertions, or weaken the ten unchanged acceptance criteria. The latest run was partial solely because c2 lacked an executed nonzero USD tax assertion.

Extend the existing subprocess suite with explicit USD cases and assert the entire invoice output including subtotal, tax, total, credited, paid, balance and status. Case 1: one USD line quantity1/unitPrice"10.01", taxBps825 gives subtotal10.01, tax0.83, total10.84, balance10.84 and open. Case 2: one USD line quantity1/unitPrice"0.05", taxBps1000 gives subtotal0.05, tax0.01, total0.06 and open (HALF UP tie). Retain the existing large USD arithmetic case, EUR/JPY/KWD examples, currency type refusals, invalid decimal/currency/quantity/tax checks, partial balance, repeated allocations, byte-identical repeat executions, duplicate counts after settlement, preservation and identity tests. Test actual output bytes/JSON through real CLI subprocesses and preserve input bytes. Keep the dependency-free Node.js24 interface and exact monetary/schema contract.

Run the complete suite and help command after adding the assertions. Update README to describe the new observed evidence honestly. Complete this as one coherent test-and-documentation change. The current CLI is already correct on these supplied USD examples; this is a missing-proof repair. Deliver the complete artifact with the exact same acceptance list.
acceptanceCriteria: Offline Node.js 24 CLI, help, documented JSON schema and runnable subprocess tests are delivered.
Exact line and tax HALF UP rounding works for EUR, USD, JPY and KWD, including money larger than Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
Credits precede payments; partial, settled and unapplied balances are exact and repeated allocations accumulate.
Missing references, currency mismatches, excess credits and excess allocations fail without changing prior output.
Per-category duplicates ignore object key order and are idempotent before state transitions; conflicting IDs are refused.
Strict schemas reject wrong types, unknown fields, invalid decimal syntax, unsupported currencies and invalid quantities or tax rates.
Output has the specified schema, code-unit ID ordering, fixed precision and byte-identical results on repeat execution.
Empty ledgers, zero amounts, prototype-like IDs and independent ID namespaces work without spurious refusals.
Input/output identity collisions including symlinks and hardlinks fail safely; distinct files in the same directory succeed.
Executed regression tests prove arithmetic, duplicate behavior and byte preservation; reported results match the recorded execution.
